reviews.body:
> [!IMPORTANT] > The fix is correct for `DurableFuture` and `DurableCallFuture`, but it fails `steep check`: `settle` is not declared in `sig/restate.rbs`. `CombinedFuture` also still returns `nil` on a second `await` after a non-terminal error. **Approach:** sound. Caching the non-terminal exception is the only option, since the VM notification is single-shot. Putting the logic in one shared `settle` helper removes the duplicated `rescue`/`ensure` code. The `CombinedFuture` combinator in the same file still has the old pattern, though. **Reviewed changes** I reviewed the whole diff and ran the new spec (3/3 pass), RuboCop (clean) and `steep check` (3 problems, 2 of them errors) locally. - **`settle` helper**: `resolve!` and `resolve_call!` now go through `settle`, which caches any `StandardError` in `@error` and re-raises it, so every `await` after a failure raises the same error. - **Spec**: `spec/durable_future_serde_spec.rb` awaits twice after a serde failure on both future types, and checks that a `TerminalError` is cached without calling `resolve_handle` again. Both failing PR checks (`Build, lint, typecheck & test` and `verify / verify`) fail during the actions lockfile check, because the `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` pin has moved. CI never ran any Ruby code, so the type error below has not been reported there. ### ⚠️ `CombinedFuture` still returns `nil` on a second `await` after a non-terminal failure `CombinedFuture#resolve_combined!` uses the same `rescue TerminalError` / `ensure @resolved = true` pattern this PR replaces. When a child raises a non-terminal error, for example a serde failure surfaced by `finalize_all_completed` or `finalize_first_succeeded` (both rescue only `TerminalError`), the first `await` raises and the second returns `nil`. I reproduced this on the PR head: `Restate.all_settled`-style (`:all_completed`) over a child with a failing serde gives `raised ArgumentError: bad payload`, then `returned nil`.
Technical details ````markdown # CombinedFuture still loses non-terminal failures on re-await ## Affected sites - lib/restate/durable_future.rb:189-196 — `resolve_combined!` rescues only `TerminalError`; `ensure` marks the future resolved with `@value = nil`, `@error = nil` when anything else propagates. ## Required outcome - A second `await` on a `CombinedFuture` whose first `await` raised a non-terminal `StandardError` raises the same error instead of returning `nil`. - One implementation of the "record outcome" logic, shared by `DurableFuture` and `CombinedFuture` (it is not a subclass, so it cannot inherit `settle` today). ## Suggested approach - Move `settle` into a small private mixin (or a module function) in `durable_future.rb`, include it in both classes, and rewrite `resolve_combined!` as `settle { @ctx.wait_combined(tree); finalize_value }`. - Declare it in `sig/restate.rbs` for whichever owner it ends up on. - Add a `CombinedFuture` example to `spec/durable_future_serde_spec.rb` (e.g. `:all_completed` over a child with a raising serde, awaited twice). - Optional: the doc comment on `DurableCallFuture#await` (line 89, "Caches both successes and TerminalError failures") is now stale. ````

review_comments.body:
`settle` is missing from `sig/restate.rbs`, and `durable_future.rb` is in the Steep `check` list. So `bundle exec steep check` (run by `make typecheck`, which `make verify` in CI depends on) now fails with `Ruby::NoMethod` at lines 54 and 100, plus an `UndeclaredMethodDefinition` warning here. I confirmed this locally. Add the method under the `private` section of `DurableFuture` in the RBS:

```rbs
    def settle: () { () -> untyped } -> void
```

comments.body:
Thanks for the review. Pushed a follow-up commit that addresses both points from the pullfrog review:

- `settle` is now declared in `sig/restate.rbs` (it lives in a small `Settleable` module included by `DurableFuture` and `CombinedFuture`), which should clear the `steep check` errors.
- `CombinedFuture#resolve_combined!` goes through the same `settle`, so a second `await` after a non-terminal child failure re-raises instead of returning `nil`. Added a spec awaiting a combined future twice over a child with a failing serde.

The two red checks fail at the actions lockfile step (the `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` pin moved), before any Ruby runs, so they are unrelated to this change.

This follow-up was prepared with Claude Code (AI) and submitted by the account owner; the spec file passes locally (the new `CombinedFuture` example fails on 0dd1e77 and passes here) and RuboCop is clean on the touched files; `steep check` could not be run locally, so CI is its first run.
